# Letter from the Editor: Early China at 40
...
2017, Early China
https://doi.org/10.1017/EAC.2017.8

## Abstract

With this issue, Early China reaches volume 40 (2017). 1 The journal was founded by David N. Keightley (1932-2017), who died on February 23 of this year. This volume is dedicated to his memory. Keightley, a specialist in oracle-bone inscriptions and Shang dynasty history, taught in the History Department at the University of California at Berkeley from 1969 to 1998. I was a graduate student in what was then called the Department of Oriental Languages from 1966 to 1972. I had already finished my coursework when Keightley began teaching, but, in 1970-1971, he offered graduate seminars on reading oracle bone and bronze inscriptions that I attended. They were the perfect complement to Boodberg's philology and this experience was critical to the direction of my later research. Indeed, Keightley's focus on ancient inscriptions as a source material for the study of Chinese history influenced the trajectory of the entire field of early China studies in the West and gave this journal its particular character. Thus, in this volume's "Letter from the Editor," I would like to take the opportunity to reminisce a little about the period when the journal was founded and to make some personal observations about the future of the field.

## Key takeaways
AI

- The journal Early China celebrates its 40th volume in 2017, honoring founder David N. Keightley's legacy.
- Keightley's work on oracle-bone inscriptions significantly shaped early China studies in the West.
- Archaeological discoveries are rapidly transforming the understanding of early Chinese civilization and its textual traditions.
- New scientific technologies are enhancing archaeological research, providing unprecedented insights into ancient populations.
- The integration of diverse knowledge types is crucial for advancing the study of early Chinese history.
...
## What were the implications of the 1973 Mawangdui tomb discoveries for early Chinese texts?add

The discovery of silk texts at Mawangdui in 1973 revolutionized our understanding of ancient Chinese texts, particularly those regarding practical writings like laws and household registries. These texts provide critical insights into social history during the early Han Dynasty.

## How has archaeological discovery transformed early China studies post-1990?add

Since the 1990s, rapid economic development in China has led to significant archaeological discoveries, many in historically important areas. These discoveries have reached a critical mass, enriching our understanding of ancient populations and fostering international scholarly exchanges.

## Why is the collaboration between Western and Chinese scholars significant now?add

The collaboration has fostered a truly global field of early China studies as Western sinology is translated into Chinese and vice versa. Young scholars now commonly spend years studying in both regions, enhancing research quality and cross-cultural understanding.

## What novel methodologies are emerging in the study of early Chinese archaeology?add

Recent methodologies include the application of scientific technologies like DNA analysis, stable isotope analysis, and satellite imagery, enhancing interpretations of archaeological findings. These techniques are transforming our comprehension of ancient Chinese populations and their interactions.

## How are searchable databases changing the analysis of transmitted texts?add

Searchable databases are revolutionizing the analysis and collation of transmitted texts with excavated materials, enabling more nuanced research. This integration is expected to significantly alter our knowledge across various aspects of early Chinese civilization.

# Early China

《Early China》是由美国汉学家基德韦教授于1975年创刊的跨学科学术期刊，研究时间跨度覆盖旧石器时代至东汉末年（公元220年） [1]。该期刊聚焦考古学、历史学、哲学、宗教、文学与古文字学等领域 [11] [13]，通过出土文献与传世典籍相结合的跨学科方法，构建早期中国文明的多元认知体系 [1]。期刊现由剑桥大学出版社出版，是A&HCI来源期刊，也是目前唯一专门研究早期中国的英文期刊 [9]。审稿流程实行双盲评审制，截至2024年累计发表量达386篇 [2]。

期刊最初聚焦于青铜时代至汉代的政治制度研究，随着考古发现增多，逐步扩展至物质文化、宗教信仰等多元领域 [4-5]。2021年李峰在序言中重申期刊使命，强调通过跨学科对话重构古代中国认知框架。期刊长期收录国际学者的前沿研究成果，如武致知对战国文本载体转型的研究、李峰关于比较文明框架的论述等 [3-5]，2025年亦有武汉大学博士研究生杨汇垚在该刊发表论文 [9] [14]。“早期中国”一词源于英文Early China的译介，其中文名“古代中国”在中文语境中存在不同理解 [7] [18]。

## 办刊历史

1975年，由美国汉学家吉德炜（David N. Keightley，也译作基德韦）创立 [1] [3-4] [6-7] [9] [17] [19]。期刊的英文名“Early China”及其中文译名“早期中国”的概念源于西方汉学界，旨在研究从史前到东汉末年（公元220年）的中国 [7] [12] [16]。期刊最初由“早期中国研究会”（Society for the Study of Early China）出版，后改由剑桥大学出版社（Cambridge University Press）出版 [8] [13] [15]。创刊宗旨为传播早期中国研究的新理论与方法论 [1] [4]。
...
2021年李峰在序言中重申期刊使命，强调通过跨学科对话重构古代中国认知框架 [4]。有学者指出，该刊中文名常被译为“古代中国”，但此译法与中文语境下“古代”的宽泛时间范围（通常至1911年）不完全相符 [7] [18]。

该期刊由早期中国研究学会出版。 [13]
